subject: The best smooth function for the temporal component

messages.author: f97b0bfe799a761a
messages.subject: The best smooth function for the temporal component
parts:
Hello!

I have a doubt about with is the best way to model the temporal component, considered as a random effect, in a spatio-temporal model. Since now I have always used the smooth function "rw1" but I have also seen in different articles the use of the "ar1". Which are the main reasons of choosing one or another?

formula1 = Y ~f(field, model=spde,diagonal=diag.eps)+f(year,model="ar1", diagonal=diag.eps)+ var1 +var2 + var3

or

formula1 = Y ~f(field, model=spde,diagonal=diag.eps)+f(year,model="rw1", diagonal=diag.eps)+ var1 +var2 + var3

Thank you very much,

Laura.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The best smooth function for the temporal component
parts:
For equally spaced time points, the difference is that RW1 is the limiting case of AR(1) where the parameter goes to 1. Ar1 is stationary, rw1 is only intrinsically stationary.  Ar1 is "pulled back" towards zero, rw1 is invariant to adding an arbitrary constant (but normally a sum-to-zero constraint is imposed on rw1, to avoid overparameterising the linear model).  

Finn
